title: Rootward
role: The title screen and the menus between runs: the main theme, in full. A confident anthem with a groove from its first bar: the game's front door, bright and solid, that makes a player want to go down again.
theme: The motif (1 5 1 3 2 1: D A D F# E D) is the hook: whistled in the intro, stated boldly in the verse, climbed a fourth in the chorus (G D G B A G), on B minor in the chorus's fifth bar, an octave up in the final chorus, and sung down as the bridge's top line (F# E D).
reference: The old music-title was a harp-and-cello meander with no pulse to tap: it repeated almost nothing (0.11), had a centroid of 490 Hz and nothing above 5 kHz, so it sounded like a lullaby, and the player found the menus too lullaby-like. This take answers that with a groove from bar one (strummed guitar, upright bass and drums at 104 BPM), a motif that returns as the hook of every section, a fiddle and flute melody in place of the harp, and a brass final chorus for a fuller, brighter sound.
form: silence 1, intro 4 (a whistled hook over the groove, which starts with the first bar), verse 8 (the motif, bold, fiddle and guitar), verse 8 (answered, flute and strings), pre-chorus 4 (the lift), chorus 8 (the hook, full band), bridge 8 (G major, rising, horns), chorus 8 (the final chorus: an octave up, horns, big), outro 4 (back to the tonic)
style: lantern folk anthem, video game title music, instrumental, no vocals, strummed acoustic guitar, upright bass, live drums with a steady foot-tapping backbeat, fiddle and wooden flute melody, accordion, bold French horns in the final chorus, confident and warm, punchy full bright mix, D major, 104 BPM
